header.name: Mahindra and Mahindra Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Mahindra and Mahindra (NSE: M&M) makes and sells automobiles and farm equipment, and runs financial services and other businesses; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹1,98,639 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹57,553 crore, 24.8% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 14.6% against 15.7%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹4,588 crore, 24.9% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 5 Nov 2026, the first session after the result, M&M shares rose 5.59% while the NIFTY 50 rose 2.40% and the NIFTY AUTO index rose 4.14%; allowing for the market's move, M&M's own move was +2.16%, about 1.82 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the autos sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹3,339 (NSE close, 16 Nov 2026), the reinvestment-phase discounted cash flow model (Template B, since M&M's median return on invested capital of 13.0% is above its 11.96% cost of capital) matches the price if revenue grows about 49.8% a year for five years at the FY26 operating margin of 14.9%; M&M's revenue grew 17.9% a year over FY23–FY26.

claims.label: INTERPRETATION
claims.text: Mahindra & Mahindra's consolidated accounts include a financial services business that lends to customers. The model counts that lender's borrowings as debt and its loan book as invested capital, so the growth read from the price here is overstated for the automotive and farm businesses.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: With the other assumptions at base, the valuation is most sensitive to how much capital each rupee of new sales needs (a quarter either way: a model value of ₹476 to ₹1,840 a share) and to the operating margin (two percentage points either way: a model value of ₹754 to ₹1,903 a share); the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹5 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, plus investments in joint ventures and associates, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹48k crore of cash and treasury.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY23–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY23 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of M&M's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.what: Revenue keeps its FY23-FY26 growth rate for five years, the FY26 margin holds, and M&M keeps its historical return on capital indefinitely.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.what: Revenue grows 2 points a year faster than its FY23-FY26 rate for five years and the margin rises 1 point.

valuation.rule_note: The cost of debt and long-run growth are set by fixed rules and not reviewed by a person.

template_b.name: Template B · reinvestment phase
template_b.why: Template A needs free cash flow to the firm to be positive in at least three of the last four years, and here it was −₹7,538 crore in FY24, ₹205 crore in FY25 and ₹3,350 crore in FY26.
template_b.test: Template B runs the same model but asks a different question of the past: does the capital being reinvested earn more than it costs? The median return on invested capital over FY24–FY26 was 13.0%, against a cost of capital of 11.96%. Its bear and bull cases are set around the history growth rate, because the latest years are the reinvestment itself.
tiles: economic profit after year 10, today's value
template_b.first_positive: In the base case, free cash flow turns positive in FY34: until then the growth is paid for by reinvestment, while economic profit is already positive.

flags.title: A lending business is inside these numbers
flags.text: Mahindra & Mahindra's consolidated accounts include a financial services business that lends to customers. The model subtracts that lender's borrowings as debt and counts its loan book as invested capital, so the growth the price implies is overstated for the automotive and farm businesses on their own. The project has no template for lenders: read this page as an illustration of that limit, not as a measure of the company.

flags.title: Terminal value is more than the whole value
flags.text: In the base and bull cases the first ten years of cash flow are negative (the lending business keeps growing its loan book), so the terminal value is more than 100% of the enterprise value. That is arithmetic, not a bug, and it is another sign that the model does not fit this company.

flags.title: The reinvestment version of the model is used
flags.text: Template A did not apply (free cash flow not positive in at least 3 of the last 4 years), so this page uses Template B, which is judged on return on capital and assumes today's return on capital lasts.

flags.title: The exchange's files contain errors
flags.text: 15 reconciliation checks fail on the exchange's own files, each with a recorded reason. They are marked as explained, not passed, and the figure as filed is used, never a corrected one.

flags.title: A revenue line was regrouped
flags.text: A small amount was regrouped between revenue and a line for losses on group investments after the June 2025 quarter was first filed, so quarters as first filed do not sum exactly to later cumulative figures. The checks are shown as explained, not repaired.

limitations: Template B (reinvestment phase): the same single-stage fade model, judged on return on capital rather than past free cash flow. The base case assumes today's return on capital lasts; no currency driver.
Cash flows are discounted to the balance-sheet date, 30 Sep 2026, two months before the price date; the model does not roll that gap forward, so its values are slightly low against the price.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The risk-free rate is a twelve-month average while the price and equity risk premium are point-in-time.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.

Mahindra & Mahindra consolidates a financial services business, a lender. Its borrowings fund loans to customers, yet the model subtracts every consolidated borrowing as debt and treats the loan book as invested capital, and lending shows up as negative operating cash flow. The growth the price implies is therefore overstated, and the model range understated, against a reading of the automotive and farm businesses alone. This project has no template for lenders: read this page as an illustration of that limit, not as a measure of the company.

Mahindra & Mahindra regrouped a small amount between revenue and a line for losses on group investments after first filing the June 2025 quarter. The exchange files carry only each filing's own columns, so quarters as first filed do not sum exactly to the later cumulative figures; the checks are shown as explained.
From FY23 the figures come from the exchange XBRL filings; the lease liabilities for FY22 to FY25 come from the results PDFs (text layers checked against the printed subtotals).
Static page: prices are end-of-day as of the date shown, not live.
